public_rationale: The May 2022 study coauthored by van den Broeck found that BERT achieved near-perfect test accuracy but failed when sampling changed within the same logical problem space [e4]. An independent April 2018 study found that inference labels could often be predicted without reading the premise, and that high-performing models did much worse on examples where this shortcut failed [e5]. Together, these studies establish repeated cases of benchmark success without reliable mastery of the intended task, including the named example [e4, e5].
limitations: The studies cover selected logical-reasoning and language-inference tasks, not all AI benchmarks or models [e4, e5].
They do not establish that the tested models learned nothing useful [e4, e5].
The assessed version of the van den Broeck study was a preprint [e4].

evidence.locator: Section 4, BERT Learns Statistical Features, opening sentence
evidence.explanation: Zhang and colleagues, including van den Broeck, found near-perfect performance within a training distribution but substantial failures under different sampling of the same logical problem space. Their analysis attributes this to statistical features rather than acquisition of the intended reasoning procedure.

Gururangan and colleagues found that labels could often be predicted without the premise needed for genuine inference. High-performing models also performed much worse on the subset where that shortcut failed, providing an independent earlier example.
